name: sql-errorlog
description: SQL Server ERRORLOG / Agent log / Windows Application event entries. Pages on corruption and data-loss risk, drops login-audit and startup chatter.

category.instructions: What kind of SQL Server event does this log entry describe?

criteria.corruption: DBCC CHECKDB errors, checksum or torn-page failures, error 823/824/825, suspect pages, msdb.dbo.suspect_pages entries
criteria.io_latency: I/O requests taking longer than 15 seconds, stalled I/O, storage path or disk problems
criteria.backup_restore: Backup or restore failures, missing log backups, VDI/VSS snapshot errors
criteria.availability: Always On availability group, mirroring, log shipping or cluster role changes, failover, disconnected replicas, redo/send queue problems
criteria.resource_pressure: Memory grant waits, non-yielding scheduler, low virtual memory, tempdb or log file full (error 9002), autogrowth storms
criteria.deadlock_blocking: Deadlock graphs, lock timeouts, long blocking chains
criteria.security: Login failures (error 18456) from unexpected sources, permission denied, certificate or TDE key problems
criteria.agent_job: SQL Server Agent job or step failures
criteria.startup_config: Service start/stop, configuration changes, trace flags, recovery progress messages
criteria.informational: Routine success messages, successful backups, log rotation, login audit success, anything with no operational consequence

severity.instructions: How operationally severe is this entry for a production database server?
criteria: Low: worth noting, no user impact
Medium: degraded or at risk, needs attention today
High: outage, data loss risk, or corruption; needs attention now

data_loss_risk.instructions: Does this entry indicate that data could be lost or is already damaged (corruption, failed log backups breaking the chain, a full transaction log, a replica that cannot catch up)?

needs_human.instructions: Would an experienced DBA need to take a manual action because of this entry, as opposed to it resolving on its own?
